Subject: DPA: SCCs and controller/processor mapping for pilot integration

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week — Calyx is excited about the pilot. Legal has a couple of items they need clarified before we can start the PO: primarily the controller/processor mapping in the MSA + Order Form, and our EU transfer approach (SCCs + any transfer-impact addendum).

Specific asks from our side:
- Confirm whether Redwood will be a processor for the pilot data or a co-controller for any telemetry/usage metrics collected.
- Provide the baseline SCCs clause you plan to include (or confirm you accept the standard EU Commission SCCs).
- If you expect to rely on derogations or other transfer mechanisms, share the transfer-impact addendum draft.

Can you send a redline or short note on these points? Procurement would like an initial response by end of week so we can unblock internal approvals. I attached our standard DPA questions for reference.

Attachments: calyx_dpa_questions.pdf (8 pages)

Best,

Hi Emma — thanks for sending this through and for the clear list.

Looping in Ben (contracts), Laura (privacy counsel) and Soojin (security/compliance) to draft a concise response + a redline of the DPA with the SCCs reference. We believe Redwood will act as processor for customer data in the pilot; we do capture telemetry for service health that is aggregated and described in the Order Form (we can mark that data as service metrics and provide options if Calyx prefers not to have it collected).

We will:
1) Share a redline of our standard DPA with SCCs called out.
2) Produce a short transfer-impact addendum draft if any hosting routes or subprocessors could require additional mitigation.
3) Confirm controller/processor language for both the MSA and Order Form.

Target: internal draft to you for review by end-of-day Thursday, Sep 16. If that timing doesn't work, let me know and we'll expedite.

Subject: RE: DPA redline prep for Calyx — initial notes and attachments

Team — attaching a first-pass redline (dpa_sccs_redline_v1.docx) and a short summary (redline-summary.txt). Key points called out in the summary:
- We should maintain "Processor" posture for the MSA/Order Form for the pilot; propose explicit language that telemetry is operational metrics under Section X, collected as aggregated, and not used to train models.
- We recommend referencing the 2021 EU Commission SCCs and adding a narrow transfer-impact addendum that documents hosting regions and subprocessor list. That addendum will also include fallback routing (EU-only) in case a subprocessor changes.
- Proposed small concession: add a 30-day notice for new subprocessors and a documented evidence package on request (SCCs + SOC2 link).

Open legal questions for Laura:
- Do we accept Calyx's proposed 3rd-party processor carveouts? (see p3 of their questions)
- Is the 30-day notification enough or do we need a 14-day window + escalation clause?

Attachments: dpa_sccs_redline_v1.docx, redline-summary.txt

Thanks — Ben
